source_spans.locator: PNAS 105(38), published p.14325, Abstract: 2,500 studied items over 5.5 h followed by paired recognition tests and 92/88/87% performance
PNAS 105(38), published p.14325, Results: two-alternative forced-choice design with novel, exemplar, and state/pose foil conditions
PNAS 105(38), published pp.14327-14329, Discussion/Conclusion: single-viewing detail retention at large scale; result is a lower bound, not an upper bound

provenance.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

conditions: single presentation of 2,500 distinct real-world item images with instructions to retain visual detail
task: two-alternative recognition comparisons using novel-category, same-category exemplar, and same-item state-or-pose foils
temporal_scope: study stream lasting about 5.5 hours followed by recognition testing; additional within-stream repeats span up to about two hours

nodes.description: large set of individually presented real-world item images
similarity class relating the previously presented item to its paired foil
two-alternative test requiring selection of the previously presented image
proportion of correct selections under the three foil-similarity conditions
selection of the previously presented member of each image pair

relations.description: observed accuracy varies with how visually and categorically similar the foil is to the previously presented item
performance is evaluated by correct identification of the previously presented image in each pair
the paired-recognition probe yields the observed accuracy used to infer preservation of item-specific visual information
high accuracy despite thousands of singly presented items supplies a lower-bound observation on jointly retained quantity and visual specificity
